$description: Ripls canonical design tokens — the single source of truth for brand/neutral/semantic colors and font families across the Flutter app, server-rendered web pages, and marketing site. Palette: Ink & Sage (issue #2441, chosen from the Phase 1 choice sheet; light theme original from PR #2440's explorer, dark theme synthesized). Edit this file only; regenerate outputs with `npm run generate:design-tokens`.

serif.$description: Display and headings. Weights 400 and 700 only; no italic display type.

sans.$description: Body, labels, and UI. Weights 400-700, falling back to the platform system sans.

$glassNote: The frosted-glass material (#2770). Deliberately NOT per-theme: the sheet sits on a dark scrim that handles theme adaptation, so on-glass content is identical in light and dark (docs/client/design.md). Values here are the shipped ones, with near-identical steps collapsed — app_colors.dart previously carried 52 declarations holding ~34 distinct values, including seven names for solid white and three for the sheet fill. Alpha is encoded in #AARRGGBB.

scrim.$description: Backdrop behind the sheet, and the darkening layer inside it over bright media. Collapses the shipped 35% and 40% blacks, which were not distinguishable. Raised from 37% to 42%: the sheet composited to grey 127 on the Material date picker, where white text needs a composite no lighter than grey 119 to clear 4.5:1 and measured 3.94-4.49, and the selected-day circle measured 2.78 against a 3:1 requirement. Ten grey levels clears both. Sized from the measurement, not chosen — a model built from the shipped values predicted the circle at 2.73 against 2.78 observed.

scrim-heavy.$description: Full-screen content panels over a hero image, where the sheet scrim is not enough to keep text legible.

scrim-tint.$description: Light tint over media that must stay readable through the overlay.

surface.$description: Translucent fill of the glass sheet.

divider.$description: Internal rules and control outlines. Deliberately brighter than surface — the shipped divider was byte-identical to the sheet it divided.

fill-faint.$description: The lightest inset fill — barely-there panel tints. 29 call sites cluster at 4-6% and would double in weight if folded into `fill-subtle`.

fill-subtle.$description: Inset cards, chips, search and inline-action fields. Collapses the shipped 8%/10%/12% whites, which differ by 2 percentage points.

hairline.$description: Dividers and hairline borders on glass. Equal to `fill-subtle` in value today but a DISTINCT ROLE — a fill and a rule that happen to share a weight will not stay in step when either is retuned. This is not the 'seven names for white' problem that motivated the factoring: those seven were all the same role (text) with no distinction to make. Sized from the code rather than taste — 8 of 9 real dividers draw at 8%, while `divider` says 24%, so routing them there would have tripled every hairline.

border-soft.$description: The everyday border on glass. `border` (30%) is the emphatic edge; measured across the app, most real borders sit at 18-20%.

border-active.$description: Border of a selected or active control on glass. Rare but real — without it a selection outline has to reach for `fill-strong`, a FILL token, which is how #2764 started.

on-fill-strong.$description: Text and icons on a fill-strong control.

drag-handle.$description: The pill at the top of a sheet.

text-secondary.$description: Secondary on-glass text. The shipped ramp had four names for solid white, so hierarchy existed in the names and never reached a pixel.

text-muted.$description: The step between `text-secondary` and `text-faint`, for supporting copy that is de-emphasised but still readable. It exists because the ramp had a hole: real call sites cluster at 60-75% and the only options were 90% or 50%, so anything in that band had to round to a weight it was never designed for. Matches `overlay.text-faint` in value, which is deliberate — the same copy often moves between a sheet and a photo.

text-faint.$description: De-emphasised on-glass text and chevrons. Never body copy.

primary.$description: On-glass action colour — the LIGHT sage, not the light-theme brand green. Glass is an always-dark material: the sheet sits on a dark scrim regardless of app theme, so a light-theme colour is wrong here by construction. It shipped as #3E5A47 (the light-theme primary) and measured 2.38:1 as a foreground on the sheet; the light sage measures 9.01:1 on the same pixels. That mismatch is what #2764 was. Note this does NOT rescue a brand colour over a mid-grey composite — on the washed photo hero the same element measures 1.50:1 light and 2.52:1 dark, because no brand green works against a mid-tone; that one is a scrim problem.

on-primary.$description: Text and icons on a primary fill. Dark, because `primary` is now light: white on the light sage measures 2.01:1, this measures 8.06:1. The pair has to move together — flipping one and not the other is how a fill and its foreground end up illegible.

secondary-border.$description: Secondary button outline, brighter so the pill shape stays unambiguous.

backdrop-blur-sigma.$description: BackdropFilter sigma for the scrim behind the sheet.

$overlayNote: The media-overlay material (#2770) — scrims and controls painted directly on user photos, on content heroes and feed cards. A separate material from `glass`: glass is a sheet floating above content, this is a wash applied to the media itself. Like glass it is NOT per-theme; the media is the backdrop and it does not follow the app theme. Previously this lived as four inline LinearGradients in widget files plus a dozen alpha values in app_colors.dart methods, which is why the sweep found 246 text-faint and 132 text-secondary failures here: every gradient fades to transparent exactly where the text sits.

scrim-top.$description: Top of the hero gradient, behind the status bar and top controls.

scrim-bottom.$description: Bottom of the hero gradient, behind the title block and metadata.

scrim-flat.$description: Flat wash over media where no gradient applies. Was 30% in light and 50% in dark; unified, because the media is the backdrop and does not follow the app theme.

wash-top.$description: Where a hero's content wash meets the top of the editorial sheet. The wash is sized to the CONTENT, not the frame, so this is the darkest the photo gets at the sheet's upper edge and everything above the run-up stays bare photograph. It has to be reached AT that edge rather than partway down: the title starts within ~16px of it, and the shipped gradient — which put transparent at the edge and 65% a fifth of the way in — left the title on roughly 10% black, measuring 3.07:1. 72% rather than that 65%: on the brightest hero photo a metadata row landed on a near-white patch and measured 3.94:1, and clearing 4.5:1 there needs 11.2% more black than 65% supplies. The threshold is 70%; the extra 2 points are margin. It costs little because everything it darkens is behind the sheet.

wash-bottom.$description: Bottom of a hero's content wash, under the deepest metadata rows.

scrim-floor.$description: Minimum wash under ANY text on media. The shipped gradients fade to fully transparent between their stops, leaving mid-hero text on bare photo. 55% is not a taste call: white text needs a composite no lighter than grey 119 to clear 4.5:1, and over a white photo that requires at least 53% black. An earlier 35% floor measured 3.07:1 on the gear title. This is the price of assuming the worst photo — luminance-aware material selection is what would let it be conditional.

outline.$description: Borders for chips, fields and controls on media. Collapses three separately-maintained white 30% values.

chip-fill.$description: Metadata and status chips on media.

text-secondary.$description: Secondary text on media. Media text must come from THIS ramp, not the palette's — the palette's neutral steps are validated against `background`/`surface` and measure as low as 2.71:1 out here.

text-faint.$description: De-emphasised text on media. Never body copy.

$paperNote: The impact-paper material (#2770) — the warm, printed-report surface used by the impact and chart views (`app/lib/presentation/widgets/impact/`, `widgets/charts/`). It is a DELIBERATE second visual language, not stale pre-Ink&Sage leftovers: the values cluster tightly in those two directories and nowhere else, and carry author comments naming them (Coral/Sage/Gold/ember/celebrate). Left untokenized it accumulated 35 distinct values across ~230 sites with no shared theme file — every widget re-declared the palette, and `0xFF8A7968` alone appeared 53 times in 12 files. Near-identical steps are collapsed here on the same principle as `glass`. Like the palette and unlike glass/overlay it IS opaque and light-only: the impact views do not currently have a dark treatment. The `accent-*` scale is named by HUE, not by meaning: the semantic mapping (which category or metric gets which hue) lives in `app/lib/presentation/widgets/impact/impact_palette.dart`. Naming it semantically here would give one value several names — sage is simultaneously the 'giveaways' category and the CO2 screen's accent — which is exactly the failure that gave `glass` seven names for solid white. Tokens carry values; code carries meaning. The accent members must stay mutually distinct, because they appear as segments of a single chart.

surface.$description: The page itself — warm cream. Collapses #FFF9F0 and #FAF8F3, which differ from it by 2-5 and were never distinguishable.

surface-raised.$description: Inset cards and table rows on the page. Collapses #F0ECE3.

border.$description: Standard rule around cards and tables.

border-strong.$description: Emphasised edge — section boundaries and chart axes.

text-muted.$description: De-emphasised labels, units, captions. Collapses #7A756D (distance 17) and #9E9280 — three names that read as one weight.

text-faint.$description: Disabled and placeholder text. Clears 3:1 on `surface`, not 4.5:1 — never body copy.

ink.$description: Deepest ink, for headline figures. Collapses #261F14.

accent-green.$description: Chart/accent scale — deeper than sage. Collapses #6B8758, 26 away.

accent-forest.$description: Chart/accent scale — the emissions metric's identity, a saturated leaf green. NOT folded into `accent-green`: it sits 41 away, and `impact_tab_bar_test.dart` pins it as a distinct identity by name ('forest').

accent-forest-light.$description: Light end of the forest gradient; `accent-forest` is the dark end. Gradients need both ends named or half the gradient silently stops following the theme.

accent-teal-light.$description: Light end of the teal gradient; `accent-teal` is the dark end.

accent-green-strong.$description: Metric-card accent. This is Material green 800 verbatim and sits 41 from `accent-forest` — it reads as a stray framework default rather than a chosen member of this palette, and is a candidate for folding into `accent-forest`. Tokenised at its shipped value so that stays a design decision instead of a side effect.

accent-blue-strong.$description: Metric-card accent. Material blue 800 verbatim, 82 from `accent-blue` — same caveat as `accent-green-strong`.

tint-amber.$description: Pale amber wash behind a highlighted metric card. A tint, not an accent — it is a background and never carries text contrast on its own.

tint-teal.$description: Pale teal wash behind a highlighted metric card.

highlight.$description: Celebration and milestone emphasis. Collapses the #C49A2A gold.

ember.$description: Warning-weight emphasis on paper — deliberately distinct from `highlight`, which is positive.

$completionNote: The completion/fulfillment sheet material (#2770). A small brand set rather than a full material: these sheets render on always-dark glass regardless of app theme (#2492), so their surfaces, text and borders come from `glass` — only the sheet base and the three brand hues are their own. Previously all four lived as `k*` constants in `dark_check_circle.dart` alongside a `CompletionColors` class whose light-theme branches were dead code (`_isDark` is pinned to `true`).

sheet.$description: Opaque base of the completion sheet, under the glass layers.

green.$description: The confirm/success brand green for these sheets. Deliberately not the palette's `success` — that one is validated against a white page, this sits on a dark sheet.

green-light.$description: Lighter partner to `green`, for gradients and hover states.

accent-light.$description: Warm accent for celebratory moments in the completion flow.

surface.$description: Raised surface: cards, sheets, alternating sections.

border.$description: Borders and dividers; cards are bordered, not shadowed.

text-faint.$description: Faint text: placeholders, footnotes, timestamps. Clears 3:1, not 4.5:1 — never for body copy.

primary.$description: Deep sage. The only fill for buttons and primary CTAs; also passes as link/text on background.

on-primary.$description: Text and icons on primary fills.

accent.$description: Ink. Emphasis accent: headline accent words (color + underline, never italics), marketing band sections.

on-accent.$description: Text and icons on accent fills (e.g. marketing bands).

success.$description: Success status. Clear green, deliberately distinct from the sage primary.

warning.$description: Warning status. Amber-brown, distinguishable from both sage and error.

error.$description: Error status: form errors, destructive actions, failure banners.

surface.$description: Raised surface: cards, sheets, alternating sections.

border.$description: Borders and dividers; cards are bordered, not shadowed.

text-faint.$description: Faint text: placeholders, footnotes, timestamps. Clears 3:1, not 4.5:1 — never for body copy.

primary.$description: Light sage. The only fill for buttons and primary CTAs; also passes as link/text on background.

on-primary.$description: Text and icons on primary fills.

accent.$description: Chalk — the dark-theme counterpart of the ink accent. Headline accent words (color + underline, never italics).

on-accent.$description: Text and icons on accent fills.

error.$description: Error status: lightened from the legacy #D16B4E to clear 4.5:1 on dark surfaces.

info.$description: Info status: lightened from the legacy #5A7A82 to clear 4.5:1 on dark surfaces.
